newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Document shows more N.Koreans seek to flee - paper.
newsitem.headline: Document shows more N.Koreans seek to flee - paper.

text.p: A South Korean newspaper said on Tuesday it had minutes of a meeting between a Pyongyang defector marooned in the South"s Beijing embassy and U.S. intelligence officials revealing plans by other Northern officials to flee.
The leading Dong-A Ilbo newspaper said Hwang Jang-yop told U.S. and South Korean intelligence officials that five to seven senior North Korean officials were also planning to seek asylum.
South Korea"s Foreign Ministry on Monday denied similar news reports but Dong-A said it had obtained a copy of the meeting"s minutes. It said no U.S. official had met Hwang.

The newspaper said most of those planning to defect were more senior officials than Hwang, who is ranked 24th in Pyongyang"s hierarchy and the highest-ranking North Korean ever to seek asylum in the South.
In a front-page report, Dong-A Ilbo said they included a powerful official ranked around tenth in the hierarchy.

"Hwang met four U.S. officials and five South Korean officials for 35 minutes at the South Korean mission in Beijing on the same day he arrived there to seek asylum," a Dong-A Ilbo official told Reuters.
"We get calls from intelligence officials here about the report but they don"t deny it," he said, asking not to be identified.
The U.S. officials who met Hwang included three from the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). They were chiefs of CIA"s Far East, Seoul and Beijing branches, he added.

Hwang, a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il and chief architect of Juche, or self-reliance, ideology, has been in the consular section of the South Korean embassy since Wednesday while China agonises over his fate.
Seoul has said Hwang sought asylum in South Korea, but North Korea has said Seoul kidnapped him.
The newspaper report said the list of the senior North Korean officials was delivered to the CIA officials but did not publish the names.
The Dong-A official declined to give the list to Reuters.
Hwang told the meeting that those who plan to flee supported reforms to open up the Stalinist state.
"I consulted with them before I defected and I came out as a representative," Hwang was quoted as telling the meeting.
